stem: Leela measures a small plastic bead. Its mass is 15 g and its volume is 20 cm³.

parts.text: What is the density of the bead?

options.text: The density of the bead is 0.75 g/cm³.
The mass of the bead is 0.75 g/cm³.
The density of the bead is 15 g/cm³ because volume need not be used.
The density is 0.75 g/cm³ for any plastic object of any size.

parts.text: State the relationship you used to find the density.

part_answers.answer: Density equals mass divided by volume: 15 g / 20 cm³ = 0.75 g/cm³.

teacher.key_rationale: Density is mass divided by volume, so 15/20 = 0.75 g/cm³ for this bead. Calling that value the mass swaps the term; omitting volume, or applying the same density to every plastic object, misses the hinge.
